launchd.summary: The very first process (PID 1). It starts, supervises and restarts every other background service and login item on macOS.
launchd.why: The foundation of macOS; nothing else can start without it. Every Mac runs one system launchd plus one per logged-in user.
launchd.quit: Never. Killing it will crash or restart the machine/session.

kernel_task.summary: The macOS kernel itself, shown as a process so its CPU use is visible. It also handles drivers and thermal management.
kernel_task.why: It is the operating system core. High CPU here is usually the kernel deliberately idling the CPU to cool the machine (thermal throttling), or heavy I/O or driver work.
kernel_task.quit: Cannot be quit. If it is busy, look for what is heating the Mac (blocked vents, a runaway app, a hub or display).

WindowServer.summary: Draws everything on screen: composites windows, handles the cursor and talks to the display and GPU.
WindowServer.why: Required for any graphical session. Its CPU use rises with many windows, high-resolution or multiple displays, transparency and animation.
WindowServer.quit: Killing it logs you out immediately and loses unsaved work.

loginwindow.summary: Manages your login session: starts your login items, shows the login/lock screen and the Force Quit window, and handles logout and shutdown.
loginwindow.why: One runs for every logged-in user session.

Finder.summary: The macOS file manager and desktop.
Finder.why: Launched automatically at login. Also powers the desktop icons and many open/save dialogs.
Finder.quit: Safe. macOS restarts it automatically (this is what 'Relaunch' in Force Quit does).

Dock.summary: The Dock, Mission Control, Launchpad, hot corners and the app switcher.
Dock.why: Part of the standard desktop. Started automatically at login.
Dock.quit: Safe. It relaunches itself within a second.

SystemUIServer.summary: Hosts menu bar extras such as the clock, Wi-Fi, volume and battery items.
SystemUIServer.why: Part of the standard desktop; started at login.

ControlCenter.summary: The Control Center menu bar item and the status icons next to it (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound, Focus, and so on).
ControlCenter.why: Part of the standard macOS desktop since Big Sur.

NotificationCenter.summary: Delivers notification banners and hosts the Notification Center and widgets.
NotificationCenter.why: Part of the standard desktop; started at login.

Spotlight.why: Started at login so search opens instantly.

mds.summary: Spotlight's metadata server: coordinates indexing of files on your disks so search can find them.
mds.why: Runs at all times. It gets busy after installing software, OS updates, plugging in drives or creating many files.
mds.quit: Don't kill it; it restarts. To stop heavy indexing, exclude folders in System Settings > Siri & Spotlight > Search Privacy.

mds_stores.summary: Stores and queries the Spotlight index database on disk.
mds_stores.why: Works alongside mds. Heavy CPU/disk use usually means a re-index is in progress.
mds_stores.quit: It restarts automatically. Indexing normally settles down on its own within minutes to hours.

mdworker_shared.summary: Spotlight importer worker: reads files (documents, mail, photos…) to extract text and metadata for the index.
mdworker_shared.why: Spawned on demand by mds. You may see many briefly, especially after big file changes or installs.
mdworker_shared.quit: Safe, but mds will just start new ones.

mdworker.summary: Spotlight importer worker: reads files to extract content and metadata for search.
mdworker.quit: Safe, but it will be restarted.

cfprefsd.summary: The preferences daemon. Every app that reads or writes settings (UserDefaults, plist preferences) goes through it.
cfprefsd.why: Always running, as both system and per-user instances.
cfprefsd.quit: Don't. It restarts instantly, and killing it risks losing very recent setting changes.

distnoted.why: Always running; one for the system and one per user.

trustd.summary: Evaluates certificate trust (TLS/HTTPS, code signing) and checks revocation status.
trustd.why: Any time an app makes a secure connection or verifies a signature, it asks trustd.

syspolicyd.summary: Gatekeeper and notarization policy daemon. Decides whether a downloaded app may run and checks it against Apple's malware and notarization data.
syspolicyd.why: Runs constantly. It can use CPU the first time you launch new or big apps while they are scanned.
syspolicyd.quit: Don't; it protects you from untrusted software.

amfid.summary: Apple Mobile File Integrity daemon. Validates code signatures for every program the system launches.
amfid.why: A core part of macOS code-signing enforcement.

logd.summary: The unified logging daemon. Collects log messages from the system and all apps.
logd.why: Always running. High CPU often means some process is logging excessively.
logd.quit: Don't; it restarts, and the logs are lost.

powerd.summary: Power management: sleep/wake, battery and power assertions that keep the Mac awake.

configd.summary: System Configuration daemon: manages network configuration, interfaces, DNS and VPN state.
configd.quit: Don't; it will break networking until restart.

notifyd.summary: Delivers low-level system notifications between processes (the notify(3) mechanism).

fseventsd.summary: File system events daemon. Tells apps (Spotlight, Time Machine, Dropbox, IDEs) when files change.
fseventsd.why: Always running. Heavy use usually reflects busy file activity such as builds or syncing.

diskarbitrationd.summary: Detects disks and volumes (USB drives, disk images, SD cards) and mounts them.

hidd.summary: Human Interface Device daemon: handles keyboard, mouse and trackpad input events.

coreaudiod.summary: Core Audio daemon. Handles all sound input and output and audio devices.
coreaudiod.why: Always running. Restarting it is a known fix for audio glitches.
coreaudiod.quit: Safe if sound is misbehaving: it restarts automatically (audio drops for a moment).

bluetoothd.summary: Bluetooth daemon: manages pairing and connections to headphones, keyboards, mice and phones.
bluetoothd.why: Always running when Bluetooth is available.
bluetoothd.quit: Safe to kill as a Bluetooth troubleshooting step; it restarts.

sharingd.summary: Powers AirDrop, Handoff, AirPlay receiving and other sharing features.
sharingd.why: Runs so nearby devices can find and share with your Mac.
sharingd.quit: Safe; it restarts. Disable AirDrop/Handoff to reduce its activity.

rapportd.summary: Continuity daemon. Links your Mac to nearby Apple devices for Handoff, Universal Clipboard, iPhone Mirroring and Auto Unlock.
rapportd.why: Runs when other Apple devices on your account are around. It often holds open local network connections.

identityservicesd.summary: Handles registration and messaging for iMessage and FaceTime and other Apple identity services.
identityservicesd.why: Runs for Messages/FaceTime and Continuity features.

apsd.summary: Apple Push Notification service daemon. Keeps a persistent connection to Apple so apps can receive push notifications.
apsd.why: Always running. Its connection to Apple servers (port 5223 or 443) is normal.

nsurlsessiond.summary: Performs background network transfers (downloads, uploads) on behalf of apps, even when they aren't running.
nsurlsessiond.why: Spawned for app updates, iCloud transfers, podcasts and similar tasks.

cloudd.summary: iCloud / CloudKit daemon. Syncs data for apps that use iCloud.
cloudd.why: Runs when you are signed in to iCloud.

bird.summary: iCloud Drive sync daemon. Uploads and downloads files in iCloud Drive and Desktop & Documents.
bird.why: Runs when iCloud Drive is enabled. High activity is normal while syncing.
bird.quit: Safe; it restarts and resumes syncing.

accountsd.summary: Manages internet accounts (iCloud, Google, Exchange) and their credentials for system apps.
accountsd.why: Runs when apps need account access.

UserEventAgent.summary: Watches for system events (hardware changes, network changes, calendar alarms) and triggers launchd jobs in response.

coreservicesd.summary: Core Services daemon: supports Launch Services and legacy application management.

lsd.summary: Launch Services daemon. Knows which app opens which file type and handles app registration.

runningboardd.summary: RunningBoard: tracks app states (foreground, background, suspended) and manages their resources and priorities.

ReportCrash.summary: Writes crash reports when a program crashes.
ReportCrash.why: Starts after an app or process crashes. Frequent appearances mean something keeps crashing.
ReportCrash.quit: Safe, but check what is crashing (Console.app > Crash Reports).

spindump.summary: Samples what a process was doing when it hung, for 'spin' and hang reports.
spindump.why: Started when an app becomes unresponsive.

tccd.summary: Transparency, Consent & Control daemon. Enforces privacy permissions (camera, microphone, files, screen recording, and so on).
tccd.why: Always running. It is what shows 'App wants to access…' prompts.

secd.summary: Keychain and iCloud Keychain syncing daemon.
secd.why: Runs when apps access the Keychain.

securityd.summary: Security daemon: handles Keychain access and cryptographic services.

pboard.summary: The pasteboard (clipboard) server. Copy and paste go through it.

universalaccessd.summary: Accessibility services: Voice Control, Zoom, keyboard accessibility and apps that control the UI.
universalaccessd.why: Runs when accessibility features are on, or when apps use the Accessibility API (automation, window managers, text expanders).

mediaremoted.summary: Handles media key and Now Playing control (play/pause keys, Control Center media controls).

photolibraryd.summary: Photos library service. Manages the Photos database.
photolibraryd.why: Runs when Photos is open or syncing.

photoanalysisd.summary: Analyses your photos in the background: faces, scenes, objects and Memories.
photoanalysisd.why: Runs when the Mac is idle and plugged in after new photos are added. Can use a lot of CPU for hours.

backupd.why: Runs hourly when Time Machine is on and the backup disk is available.

softwareupdated.summary: Checks for and downloads macOS and Apple app updates.

mobileassetd.summary: Downloads and manages system assets such as dictionaries, fonts, Siri/ML models and voices.

locationd.summary: Location Services daemon. Combines Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and GPS data to work out where the Mac is.
locationd.why: Runs when Location Services is on.
locationd.quit: Don't; manage it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services.

mDNSResponder.summary: Bonjour and DNS resolver. Resolves host names and discovers printers, AirPlay speakers and other local devices.
mDNSResponder.why: Always running. Nearly every network lookup passes through it.
mDNSResponder.quit: Don't; use it only as a last-resort DNS fix (it restarts).

socketfilterfw.why: Runs when the firewall is enabled.

sandboxd.summary: App Sandbox daemon: logs and enforces sandbox policy violations.

cupsd.why: Runs when printers are configured or in use. It listens on localhost port 631.

sshd.summary: OpenSSH server. Allows remote logins to this Mac.
sshd.why: Only runs if Remote Login is enabled in System Settings > General > Sharing, or when someone connects.
sshd.quit: If you didn't turn on Remote Login, investigate who connected; turn it off in Sharing settings.

kernelmanagerd.summary: Loads and manages kernel extensions and system extensions (drivers, network filters, security tools).

sysextd.summary: System extensions daemon. Manages third-party system extensions such as VPNs, endpoint security and virtual drivers.

endpointsecurityd.summary: Mediates the Endpoint Security framework used by security tools and EDR agents.

XProtectService.summary: Scans apps with XProtect, Apple's built-in malware detection.
XProtectService.why: Runs when new software is launched.

XProtect.summary: Apple's built-in malware scanner and remediation.
XProtect.why: Runs periodically and when software is launched.

com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.summary: A web page renderer. It runs the web content for Safari tabs and for any app that embeds web views.
com.apple.WebKit.WebContent.why: One per Safari tab or embedded web view. Can be heavy if a page misbehaves.

com.apple.WebKit.Networking.summary: The network process for WebKit. It fetches web resources for Safari and embedded web views.
com.apple.WebKit.Networking.why: Runs as long as WebKit is in use.

com.apple.WebKit.GPU.summary: WebKit's GPU process. Handles graphics and video for web content.

siriknowledged.summary: Siri knowledge daemon: keeps data used by Siri suggestions and shortcuts.

suggestd.summary: Provides Siri Suggestions drawn from Mail, Messages, Calendar and other apps.
suggestd.why: Background intelligence service; indexes your content on device.

parsecd.summary: Powers Spotlight Suggestions and Siri-related lookups, sending queries to Apple's search services.
parsecd.why: Runs when Spotlight searches use online suggestions.

corespotlightd.summary: Lets apps add their own content to the Spotlight index.

fontd.summary: Font server: loads, caches and activates fonts for apps.

iconservicesagent.summary: Generates and caches app and file icons.
iconservicesagent.quit: Safe. Killing it is a common fix for corrupt icons.

dasd.summary: Duet Activity Scheduler. Decides when background tasks (backups, indexing, updates) run, based on power, thermal state and usage.

coreduetd.summary: Learns your usage patterns to predict which apps to prepare and when to run background work.

biomed.summary: Stores on-device behavioral data (Biome) used by Siri suggestions and system intelligence.

findmydeviced.summary: Find My daemon. Lets you locate, lock or erase this Mac.
findmydeviced.why: Runs if Find My Mac is enabled.

searchpartyd.summary: Find My network daemon. Helps locate lost Apple devices and AirTags via nearby devices.
searchpartyd.why: Runs if Find My is enabled.

CalendarAgent.summary: Syncs calendars and delivers event alerts.

remindd.why: Runs for Reminders and iCloud sync.

login.summary: Starts a new terminal login session.
login.why: Spawned by Terminal or SSH when a shell opens.
login.quit: Closing the terminal window ends it.

zsh.summary: The Z shell, macOS's default command-line shell.
zsh.why: Runs in each Terminal tab/window, and often inside other tools such as IDEs and Claude Code.
zsh.quit: Closing the terminal ends it; any commands running inside it will stop.

bash.why: Opened by Terminal, scripts or tools.
bash.quit: Ends whatever script or session it's running.

sudo.summary: Runs a command with administrator (root) privileges.
sudo.why: Someone or something ran `sudo ...` in a terminal.

Activity Monitor.summary: Apple's process viewer, the app that Pidwick augments.
